title: Vessel imagery and internet-cable risk scenarios — Nazar's demo pack
purpose: Offline demonstration figures: real satellite vessels with fictional identities and separately labelled simulated internet-cable/behavior overlays.
coordinate_order: Source-image pixels: [x, y] from the upper-left; bounds are [left, top, right, bottom], with right/bottom exclusive. These are not geographic coordinates.
limitations: Names and AM-IE codes are invented presentation identifiers, not verified identities, MMSIs or IMO numbers.
Vessels are selected manually from published optical imagery; no AIS association or suspicious behavior is established.
A single image cannot establish movement, loitering, AIS switch-off, spoofing or cable proximity.
Enlargement uses nearest-neighbor display; it adds no sensor detail. Published imagery is not georeferenced here and cannot supply measured vessel dimensions.
The Dublin source gives a data year of 2020 but no exact acquisition date. Its 2022 publication date is not the observation date.
Cork is a published image acquired on 23 June 2026, not live imagery.

Cable-risk figures add simulated fibre-optic cable corridors and tracks. Cable routes are illustrative pixel-space overlays, not visible seabed features or real surveyed routes; no real cable proximity or risk is measured.
